stvc_arena_favourite.description: I'll be straight with you. Your wins made my bet on you worth far more than I paid, so I sold most of my stake this morning, and the part I kept pays best if you last eleven minutes against Jen'shala and then fall. I'm telling you because you'd have found out anyway, and I'd rather it came from me. Jen'shala drains the fight out of you and strips your armour, and the house has never once put her on the sand to lose. Go down, do what you're going to do, and collect your winnings from the Quiet Man in Booty Bay.
stvc_arena_favourite.accept_text: Whatever happens down there, I won't hold it against you for long.

stvc_arena_first_four.description: I keep da arena's fight list, as my father did before me, and I don't care who wins, only dat da list is right. Before you go down, I'll tell you what nobody in Booty Bay can. You can only walk da ring one way round, because da mason never cut da other passages. First is Vek'tar da Unbeaten, and once he's worn down he starts drainin' da fight back out of you, so keep da pressure on him. Den Grateward Mok'tal, who keeps a fire burnin' under da grate and shuts down whatever you answer it with. Nobody beats Mok'tal by bein' patient.
stvc_arena_first_four.accept_text: Go down da stair into Gurbashi Arena, and walk da ring anticlockwise, always.

stvc_arena_pair.description: Now dat da bettors know whose money is on you, da arena's changed your next fight, and I'll tell you plainly it ain't my decision, but it's on my list. Da handlers have put Jin'sha in da pit with Rakjan da Ribcracker, which dey only do when da house wants a round to stop bein' predictable. Rakjan is loud, but he ain't da danger, Jin'sha is. After him comes Zul'gar Hammerfall, who guards da passage to da hall, and somebody from his family has stood in dat doorway for three generations. He swings three times, all of dem huge, and one strips your armour off.
stvc_arena_pair.accept_text: Spend da fight on da big one and you'll die to da small one. Plan for Zul'gar's third swing.

stvc_centre_gate.description: Da first fighter through da centre gate dis season never came back. His kit came back up, and we hung it on a peg and counted it, but dere's no name to write on his line, because he came from somewhere else and da column stayed blank. I've kept dis list my whole life, and dis is its first gap in three generations. Take his kitbag down past da gatekeepers to da Hard Round, da dead end in front of da centre gate, and stand where he stood. Den bring da bag back up and hang it on its peg in da gatehouse.
stvc_centre_gate.accept_text: Da gatekeepers will try to stop you. Guardin' dat spot is older than my family.

stvc_cord_sealed.description: I got da Font's readings, but I won't give dem to Overseer Mokra. Anything written down in a garrison has to be acted on by da end of da week. What dese readings need is someone whose whole trade is measurin' water, and who answers to nobody, and dere's nobody like dat in dis jungle. Bring me more cords from da Font, fresh ones, so nobody can say my numbers are a season old. Den go up to da Plunge, da lamp gallery above da pool in da Veilfall Cave, and look at da old waterline on da stone and da newer one above it.
stvc_cord_sealed.accept_text: Look at it yourself. I won't send word about somethin' you ain't seen.

stvc_crate_nail.description: You turn it over in your hand. It's a crate nail, square cut and flat headed, the kind used in shipping timber, and it's stamped with a run number. You found it on the Mosh'Ogg Shelf, up a road that only leads up. Numbered nails come in runs, and a run means a clerk somewhere wrote down where the crate went. Only one man in Stranglethorn would know a run number on sight, Clerk Bexx, behind his desk in Booty Bay, and he'll be insufferable about being asked.
stvc_crate_nail.accept_text: Deal with some of the Mosh'Ogg brutes before you head down. The nailed timber's in their camp.

stvc_drum_callers.description: The arena drums aren't just music. They're how the bettors time each round, and a round lasts as long as the drum crew says it does. I've got several afternoons of fights that ran long by exactly the same amount, and I've worked out the drum-callers are being paid off. Take them down out on the Gurbashi Flats by the gate, where the crowd can see, then get me more of the stock tallies from the crates. If I'm wrong about this, I've just had musicians killed over nothing, so I want the paper.
stvc_drum_callers.accept_text: Signed-in weight is worth more than coin down here, because nobody has to count it.

stvc_fenn_lit_fall.description: At night the curtain of the Veilfall glows, and I've told myself for two years it was moonlight on the water. Water doesn't glow like that, but lamps do. If someone's lighting lamps behind the falls, then somebody's been living in that cave the whole time I've been camped outside it. Nightpelt panthers prowl the edge of the basin at dusk, and they're the real reason I've never gone round to look. Deal with them, then walk round to the mouth of the Veilfall Cave, just south of my rack, and tell me if there's a door.
stvc_fenn_lit_fall.accept_text: I've spent two years telling myself there isn't one. Go and find out.

stvc_fenn_weather.description: I dry herbs on a rack here at the edge of the Veilfall Basin and sell them to Grom'gol. There's a moss that grows along the lip of the falls, only where the spray reaches, and I need a good batch. Clear the snapjaw leechswarms out of the slack water below the pool while you're there. Think about this on the way, because it's been bothering me. Where you come from, does the rain come in a season, or all year round? Everything I know about plants assumes a wet season and a dry one.
stvc_fenn_weather.accept_text: Pick the moss where the spray's heaviest. The dry edges are no good to me.

stvc_ganger_cut.description: My gang keeps da Vine Road clear of bloodvine, and da Gurbashi pay me for it, since nobody walks to dere arena through raw jungle. Bloodvine grows back over a cut road in about nine days, and I been short of hands since da rains. Dis road got a crown in da middle so da rain runs off, and da kerb stones hold it up, but da vine comes right through da kerb. Bring me lengths of cut vine from along it, mon. And kill dem greenwater adders while you're down dere, because dey nest in da drains and bite my boys when dey reach in.
stvc_ganger_cut.accept_text: Bring dem lengths coiled, not dragged. Dragged vine leaves seed all down da road.

stvc_ganger_milepost.description: My gang is paid by da furlong, and da mileposts along da Vine Road decide how many furlongs we cut. Da stones have stood at da kerb with dere carved faces pointin' north since my father's day. Now some of dem have been dug up and reset facin' da wrong way, by somebody who knew exactly what dey were doin'. Kill da bloodvine raptors on da road south of here and bring me more cut vine from da kerb. Den walk south along da Vine Road to da long milepost where it bends, and tell me which way da carved face is pointin'.
stvc_ganger_milepost.accept_text: North is Grom'gol. I never seen one turned in my life.

stvc_garza_report.description: I was posted from Grom'gol to watch the only road up onto the Mosh'Ogg Shelf. In my second week I dropped my spyglass into the notch, signed for and stamped with my number, and every report I've sent since has been guesswork. The Mosh'Ogg rockthrowers grab anything shiny and pile it on the midden behind their camp up here on the shelf. Put them down and bring me the made things off that pile, not the bones. If my spyglass is in there, it'll have a brass collar with my number stamped on it.
stvc_garza_report.accept_text: If it isn't there, my next report has to say something different from the last nine.

stvc_limeback_lamps.description: The glow behind the Veilfall went out four nights after the Veilspeaker died, and I've sat watching the dark water ever since. For two years I told myself nobody lived behind the falls, and now it's true, and I know why. With nobody keeping them down, the limebacks have climbed up off the lowest terrace, so stop them before they find the ramp out. Gather me more spray moss while you're at it, since I haven't stopped selling it. Then go into the Veilfall Cave, just south of here, down to the lowest terrace, where there's a jar of lamp oil under the bracket.
stvc_limeback_lamps.accept_text: The Veilspeaker told me where that oil was, the day I brought him a gift.

stvc_no_bed_between.description: I keep Grom'gol's south gate, and I count everyone who heads down the Vine Road toward Booty Bay. Two travellers went south this month and never came back past me. The Bloodvine raptors have been hunting the road where it fords the Veilfall, because it's the one spot where you have to slow down. Go down to the ford, thin them out, and while you're standing in it, look at the stones and the water around them. If somebody went into that river, I'd rather hear it from you than from their family.
stvc_no_bed_between.accept_text: Walk it properly, all the way to the ford. I'll know if you turned back at the bend.

stvc_north_leg.description: I've flown freight out of Grom'gol since the camp was one post and a rope. My route north used to cross the Veilfall Basin, where warm air lifted my wyverns over the trees, but since the falls rose the air there's turned cold. The long way round costs me a day I don't get paid for, and limewing bats from the cave have taken over the old perches. Kill them in the cave where they sleep, then stand on the old perch at the edge of the Veilfall Basin and feel the air coming off that water. This bundle from Zul'jana goes north to Ghulrak at Tarren Mill, so put it in his hands yourself.
stvc_north_leg.accept_text: Not on the perches, mind. I've got beasts on the ground there.

stvc_notch_tithe.description: My report has the crate nail in it now, proof that the Mosh'Ogg and the arena gate have been trading. A tribunal won't settle for a nail, though. They'll want the goods from the midden, the drovers who signed for the weights, and a witness they can question. Bring me more stamped goods off the Mosh'Ogg midden, then head south-west down the Vine Road to the crates and thin out the Gurbashi beast-drovers. I'll be straight with you, I can't name you as that witness, because a tribunal wants one with a village and a commander behind them.
stvc_notch_tithe.accept_text: You'll be the unnamed party who recovered the items. That's the form, not my opinion of you.

stvc_reed_verdict.description: My family's milled the Tarren Mill race for sixty years and written its height down every week in one ledger. I've laid the jungle's cords against my records, and I've found that pattern twice, but never a third time. I want a proper marker set at those falls, so somebody can measure it again. This is a gauge board, oak and numbered, cut by my father for a weir that silted up years ago. Take it to the Veilfall Basin in Stranglethorn and set it in sound stone above the falls, low enough for a short person to read.
stvc_reed_verdict.accept_text: The spraywater elementals will come up out of the water while you work. Be ready for them.

stvc_scrip_drums.description: I've never been more than a mile from the cove, but I can hear the arena drums on still nights, and I know they're made of gorilla hide. Go up the road to the arena and look at the drums for me, how many, how big, and what they're made of. And kill some of the big drumhide gorillas, because that's a clue, they're named after the drums! Bring me bits of their hide so I can feel it. Stand on the Gurbashi Flats in front of the gate too, so you can tell me how many people fit. I'll pay you by telling you which crates on the pier aren't nailed down.
stvc_scrip_drums.accept_text: Don't tell Hobb I sent you. He'll only say I'm wrong again.

stvc_scrip_second.description: I didn't like it when you told me the big drums are crocolisk belly, and I've been thinking about it for four days. I haven't come round, but I've worked out how to settle it. Kill some of the crocs in the Snapjaw Marsh, not for the hide, for how big the biggest one is. If none of them is as wide across the belly as a drum is across the top, it can't be croc, so I'm right and Hobb's wrong. That's called a test, and Clerk Bexx told me about tests.
stvc_scrip_second.accept_text: I've got questions too, and I wrote them on my hand, so don't go anywhere yet.

stvc_shelf_road.description: The Mosh'Ogg hold this shelf because there's only one notch up through the mesas, and they were standing nearest to it when it mattered. My next report will admit to the lost spyglass, and I'd like some good news in it too. Clear the maulers off the approach and the spellgorgers out of their clearing at the top. Then walk into the clearing on the Mosh'Ogg Shelf, so that someone from this post has actually stood in it this season. I've spent eleven weeks reporting on a camp I've never set foot in.
stvc_shelf_road.accept_text: I'm done guessing. Go and stand in it for me.

stvc_sluice_book.description: I work the gate on the Tarren Mill race, and when I lower it, the wheel stops and the whole valley knows my name within the hour. I've done it twenty-two years. Zul'jana's cords are flat on my bench, and I've read them twice. What I think of them, I'd rather say at the weir, with the water loud beside us. I trust what I say more when I'm standing next to the river.
stvc_sluice_book.accept_text: Come up to the weir and ask what you came to ask. Mind the walkway, because a few of those boards are new.

stvc_tout_entry.description: I take bets on the Gurbashi Arena from a board in Booty Bay's tavern, and I've already entered you in the fights without asking. Nobody down here has seen you lose, so the odds on you are generous, and I like generous odds. I need the card to be worth watching, though. Right now the Gurbashi drovers are sending underweight beasts into the pens and signing them in at full weight, and thin fights mean thin betting. Put some of the beast-drovers down here on the Gurbashi Flats, and bring me their stock tallies, the papers where they sign in the weights.
stvc_tout_entry.accept_text: Do it where the bettors can see you. I haven't decided yet whether that's good for the odds.

stvc_tout_staked.description: With my own money riding on you now, I can't walk away from a bad afternoon any more. Your entry chit has to reach the arena gatehouse before you can fight, and the Gurbashi gate crew don't take a goblin's word for anything. Take it north up the apron to Gatehouse Broker Zul'tamo and put it in his hand yourself. The gatekeepers will try to stop you, because that's what they're paid for, so fight through them. Get a look at the way into Gurbashi Arena while you're up there.
stvc_tout_staked.accept_text: Don't dawdle, because the drums start at dusk and I've got money on you being there.

stvc_ulua_cold_month.description: My marsh is brackish, and my whole trade depends on that. My nets are cut for fish that live where salt water and river meet. For about three years now, fresh water's been pushing down into the Snapjaw Marsh, and my catch has started coming up wrong. Pull the far lines this time, out where the marsh stops being mine, and clear the leechswarms out of the slack water first. Then walk south-west to the far edge of the Snapjaw Marsh, past the last stake, where the grey reeds turn green.
stvc_ulua_cold_month.accept_text: That line's moved in my lifetime. I want someone besides me to have stood on it.

stvc_ulua_netsetter.description: I've fished the Snapjaw Marsh all my life, off the same landing my mother used. My hands have been stiff since the cold month, and I can barely close them. My lines are out past the gangplank where the water goes still. Pull them, bring in the catch, and reset them exactly the way you found them. The snapjaw crocolisks have been tearing the nets to get at the fish, so deal with them too.
stvc_ulua_netsetter.accept_text: And don't tell anyone in Booty Bay you did this. I sell there.

stvc_veilspeaker.description: The Veilspeaker who leads the Zul'Rath has decided my camp is why the falls changed. His shrinekeepers came up and took my drying rack apart without a word. I went in with a gift of lamp oil to make peace, and I came back out with nothing settled. He's right that the ground is his, and I'm right that I've got nowhere else to go. I've thought about this for four days before asking. He's down in the Veilfall Cave, on the south shore of the plunge pool, so go down and end it.
stvc_veilspeaker.accept_text: Just don't tell me it was quick.

stvc_wager_slip.description: You cut it out of a crocolisk's stomach, which isn't where paper belongs. It's a betting slip, stiff with salt and brown at the folds but still readable, with a fighter's name, a round, and the odds on it. The odds are good enough that whoever held it must have known something. The handwriting is small, quick and neat, and Tout Bexxil up on the arena apron writes exactly like that. Before you take it to her, go back through the Snapjaw Marsh and look along the water by the gangplank.
stvc_wager_slip.accept_text: Kill the snapjaw crocolisks on the way. Whatever else went into that water may be inside one.

stvc_zuljana_font.description: Deep in da Veilfall Cave, at a pool called da Font, da Zul'Rath measure da falls every mornin' with a knotted cord and keep da old cords to compare. Three years ago da water rose in da wrong season, and it ain't gone back down. I want dose cords, to see how far it's changed. Go down to da Font and bring dem to me, and expect a fight while you're gatherin', because spraywater elementals rise out of dat pool. Leave da shrine alone, it ain't ours.
stvc_zuljana_font.accept_text: Don't try to read da knots. Just carry dem back and I'll do da readin'.

stvc_zuljana_names.description: I've got the cave behind the Veilfall on my map as the waterfall cave, because that's what the garrison calls it. The Zul'Rath trolls who keep it have a name carved on each of its terraces, and Zul'jana's asked me to get every one of them onto the map before the garrison's name is the only one left. Each terrace in the Veilfall Cave has a name stone set in its edge, and I need those stones. The Zul'Rath mistcallers won't let you stand on a terrace long enough to read one, so you'll have to go through them first. Zul'jana doesn't like asking that, and neither do I.
stvc_zuljana_names.accept_text: Carry dem stones flat. I need to read dem names, and a chipped edge loses a letter.

stvc_zultamo_courses.description: Zul'jana sent you to ask why da Zul'Rath word for da Veilfall's water is da same as da Gurbashi word for da arena's sand. I'm da third of my family to keep da fight list, and nobody's ever asked me dat. I put my pen down for it, and I don't do dat often. Come down da stair with me and we'll talk standin' in it, because half of what I'll tell you, you need to see. Wait at da Sand Gate, at da foot of da stair, where da ring looks like it opens both ways.
stvc_zultamo_courses.accept_text: Den ask your questions. I'll answer what I can, and be honest about what I can't.
